question: Consider an image of the flag of Tonga, and consider the matrix attained by giving every red pixel a value $a$, and every white pixel a value $b$. What is the maximal possible rank of this matrix?

2.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The matrix for the Tonga flag is formed by assigning value a to all red pixels and b to all white pixels. The dominant uniform red field contributes one constant pattern across most rows and columns. The white canton in the upper hoist-side corner introduces a distinct rectangular block of b values, adding a second independent direction. The red cross overlaid on that canton creates a third pattern consisting of the cross arms (again value a) intersecting the white rectangle. These three geometric blocks—full red field, white canton rectangle, and the cross overlay—produce row and column spaces that together span at most three dimensions; any apparent fourth direction from the cross arms is a linear combination of the existing red and white blocks, so the rank cannot exceed 3. I assign this roughly 70 % .

8.text:
The flag of Tonga consists of an overall red field containing a white canton in the upper hoist corner; a red Greek cross is centered inside the canton. The corresponding matrix \(M\) therefore takes only the two scalar values \(a\) (on all red pixels) and \(b\) (on all white pixels).  

Algebraically this matrix admits the decomposition  
\[
M=bJ+(a-b)W,
\]  
where \(J\) is the all-ones matrix (rank 1) and \(W\) is the 0-1 indicator of the white pixels. The support of \(W\) is exactly the canton rectangle minus the two arms of the cross. Each rectangle indicator is an outer product of two indicator vectors and therefore has rank 1; the cross itself is the union of two rectangles and consequently has rank at most 3. Subtracting from the canton indicator shows that \(W\) itself has rank at most 4.  

Because the four rank-1 summands that generate \(W\) are linearly dependent once they are embedded inside the larger all-red field, the column space of \(M\) collapses by one further dimension. Consequently \(\operatorname{rank}(M)\le3\) for any scalars \(a,b\).  

Choosing generic distinct values (e.g., \(a=1\), \(b=0\)) realizes rank exactly 3, which is therefore maximal.  

PUBLIC RESPONSE: 3 (pattern yields rank(M) ≤ 3; generic a ≠ b attain equality)

11.text:
The flag of Tonga consists of a red field, a white canton occupying the upper hoist-side rectangle, and a red Greek cross contained entirely inside that canton. Consequently, after discretization to an \(m \times n\) pixel grid the resulting matrix contains only two distinct numerical values: \(a\) wherever a pixel is red and \(b\) wherever a pixel is white.

All rows that lie completely outside the vertical extent of the canton are identical (the constant vector whose every entry equals \(a\)). All rows that intersect the horizontal bar of the cross are likewise identical to that same constant vector. Every remaining row (those that intersect the canton but miss the horizontal bar) is also identical to one another; each such row consists of a prefix of \(a\)'s, followed by a block pattern of the form “\(b\)'s, a vertical strip of \(a\)'s, \(b\)'s”, followed by a suffix of \(a\)'s. Hence the matrix possesses at most two distinct row vectors.

Any matrix whose rows span a space of dimension at most 2 has rank at most 2. Choosing a resolution fine enough that both row vectors actually appear and setting \(a\neq b\) makes the two vectors linearly independent, so rank exactly 2 is attained. Therefore the maximal possible rank is 2.

The flag of Tonga consists of a red field with a white canton in the upper left containing a red cross. Any pixel image of the flag can therefore be partitioned into a minimal number of uniform rectangular blocks (four distinct row-blocks and four distinct column-blocks) on which the color is constant. This yields an equivalent \(4 \times 4\) pattern matrix whose entries are drawn from the two-element set \(\{a,b\}\):

\[
\begin{pmatrix}

The two distinct rows of the pattern matrix are linearly independent whenever \(a\neq b\). Consequently the pattern matrix has rank exactly 2, and every possible pixel matrix realizing the flag has rank at most 2. The bound is attained for any choice \(a\neq b\) (for instance the canonical values \(a=1\), \(b=0\)).

Thus the maximal possible rank is 2.

11.text:
The flag geometry consists of a solid red field containing a white canton in the upper hoist, inside which a red Greek cross is centered. This partitions the canton into four rectangular white regions.  

Assigning value \(a\) to every red pixel and value \(b\) to every white pixel therefore yields the matrix  
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]  
where \(J\) is the all-ones matrix of the same dimensions and \(W\) is the 0-1 indicator whose support consists exactly of those four rectangles.  

Because the vertical arm of the cross forces the two rectangles lying above it to be identical in height to the two rectangles lying below it, the four rectangles occupy only two distinct horizontal bands. Consequently every row of \(W\) is one of two possible vectors: the zero vector (outside the canton) or the three-block pattern \((b-a,0,b-a)\) (inside the canton). These two row vectors are linearly independent whenever \(a\neq b\). Hence the row space of \(M\) is spanned by at most two vectors and  
\[
\rank(M)\le2.
\]  
Choosing \(a\neq b\) realizes equality, so the maximal attainable rank is exactly 2.  

All higher-rank claims rest on overlooking the forced repetition of the two horizontal bands and therefore on an over-estimate of the dimension of the span of the four rank-1 rectangle matrices; once that repetition is taken into account the four outer products become linearly dependent and collapse to a single additional dimension beyond the constant term.  

FINAL ANSWER: 2

FINAL ANSWER: 2

(The flag geometry produces at most two distinct row vectors when red/white pixels receive values \(a\) and \(b\): the constant-\(a\) rows that lie entirely outside the canton or coincide with the horizontal arm of the cross, and the single non-constant pattern consisting of a white rectangle segment interrupted by the vertical arm of the cross. All other rows are identical to one of these two, so the row space is spanned by a pair of vectors and the matrix rank is exactly 2 for \(a\neq b\).)
